title: sessionization-histogram-spotlight-econ-mar09-2026
body:
Purpose and quick summary:
This note captures a compact set of session-length histograms and the resulting amortized latency + per-session cost implications across two common GPU profiles (A100-80GB fp16, H100-80GB int8 path) for our conversational workloads. Aim: give product/infra pragmatic knobs (routing, prewarm, cache TTL) that materially reduce unit-cost for multi-turn users while preserving 99th percentile turn latency.

Top-line findings (actionable):
- Short sessions dominate: ~68% of sessions are 1-2 turns. Optimizing for these yields most cost savings via short-tail batching and prefix cache reuse.
- Long sessions (>10 turns) are rare (~6%) but contribute ~28% of total tokens and ~34% of total GPU time; treat these as stateful fast-paths (sticky capacity).
- H100 int8 path reduces per-token GPU time by ~22–28% vs A100 fp16 for our mix, but startup prewarm penalty on H100 is higher for single-turn bursts (add ~6–9ms).
- Recommend: route sessions with expected length >=6 to dedicated slots with sticky KV cache + keep-alive; route 1–2 turn sessions to opportunistic pooled capacity with aggressive batching and prefix cache.

Experiment setup (short):
- Workload: sampled 10k sessions from production logs (Feb 2026). Sampling stratified by customer tier (free/paid).
- Sessionization: a session = sequence of client messages + model responses with <= 30min idle gap. Turn = client message prompting a generation.
- Model binary: open-13b-derived model, ~13B weights, served with two runtime configurations: A100 (fp16 kernels) and H100 (int8 quantized execution path).
- Payload: median prompt length 35 tokens, median response 120 tokens, stdev high (fat tail).
- Serving config: batching window 10ms opportunistic, cold-cache startup measured with no prior kvcache, warm-cache measured with 90% earlier-turn prefix reuse.
- Metrics: per-turn latency P50/P95/P99, per-session amortized latency (sum of per-turn latencies), GPU-ms per session, and cost-estimated USD per session (using internal cost model: $/GPU-hour: A100=3.20, H100=4.10).

Observed session-length distribution (per 10k sessions):
- 1 turn: 4200 sessions (42%)
- 2 turns: 2600 sessions (26%)
- 3-5 turns: 2000 sessions (20%)
- 6-10 turns: 800 sessions (8%)
- 11-20 turns: 300 sessions (3%)
- 21+ turns: 100 sessions (1%)

ASCII histogram (relative):
1 | ██████████████████████████████████████ 42%
2 | ████████████████████ 26%
3-5 | █████████████ 20%
6-10 | ████ 8%
11-20 | █ 3%
21+ | ░ 1%

Per-session amortized numbers (representative buckets) — A100 vs H100:
Table: bucket, sessions/10k, avg GPU-ms/session (A100), avg GPU-ms/session (H100), est USD/session (A100 cents), est USD/session (H100 cents)
- 1-turn, 4200: A100 60ms, H100 47ms, A100 $0.000053 (0.0053c), H100 $0.000048 (0.0048c)
- 2-turn, 2600: A100 120ms, H100 94ms, A100 $0.000106, H100 $0.000096
- 3-5 turns, 2000: A100 340ms, H100 265ms, A100 $0.000300, H100 $0.000271
- 6-10 turns, 800: A100 900ms, H100 688ms, A100 $0.000795, H100 $0.000704
- 11+ turns (avg 18), 400: A100 2400ms, H100 1872ms, A100 $0.00212, H100 $0.00192

Notes on numbers: per-session GPU-ms includes kernel execution + amortized scheduling overhead. Cost calc folds in GPU utilization factor measured during runs (~72% average). H100 cost advantage per token improves with longer sessions (better packing + int8 advantages).

Latency shape & SLO implications:
- For 1–2 turn sessions, P95 is dominated by scheduler/startup jitter; improving batching/window heuristics reduces P95 by ~8–12%.
- For >6 turn sessions, tail latency mainly driven by KV cache miss at first few turns (cache warmup). Ensuring sticky routing reduces P99 by ~20–25% for these users.

Micro-visual: amortized latency vs session length (rough):
- curve rises sublinearly from 1 to 5 turns (benefit from prefix reuse), then near-linear 6–20 (less reuse as longer context), long sessions flatten due to chunking optimizations.

Recommended operational knobs (priority order):
1) Sticky fast-path for sessions predicted >=6 turns (simple heuristic: user-type + replica history); allocate 1:50 reserved slots ratio initially. Rationale: small fraction of sessions -> big share of GPU time; giving stickiness reduces repeated KV cache misses and scheduling churn.
2) Short-session pooling: optimize batching window aggressively for 1–2 turn flow (reduce window to 6–8ms during burst windows, increase opportunistic batch size limit). Saves ~9–14% cost on short-tail.
3) Prompt-path prefix caching: store common system/prompt prefixes across tenant groups with TTL=10min; observed hit-rate lift +6% for short sessions.
4) Model path selection: route long sessions to H100-int8 when available; route ultra-short single-turn traffic to pooled A100 if H100 prewarm penalty would increase P95 beyond target.
5) Telemetry: add per-session KV-cache-hit trace tag + prewarm time to logs; tie into rollout gating for any scheduling change.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Predictive heuristics: can we infer session-length after 1st turn with >70% precision? If yes, sticky routing becomes cheaper. (Experiment idea: small live bucket with simple logistic predictor).
- Cost model sensitivity: how do the numbers change with lower GPU $/hr assumptions (multi-year forecasting)? Quick sim needed for 2x/0.5x price points.
- Multi-tenant fairness: risk of starvation when we reserve slots for long sessions—compute worst-case throughput impact for 95th percentile of tenant concurrency.

Appendix: quick methodology checklist (for re-run)
- Input sample: production logs export CSV (session_id, turn_idx, user_tier, tokens_in, tokens_out, start_ts, end_ts).
- Replayer: local replayer with deterministic inter-arrival preserved; synthetic jitter added to simulate network (0–50ms).
- Runtime config: match prod kernel builds; measure cold/warm by clearing KV-store between runs.
- Cost model: GPU-time * utilization correction / 3600 * $/GPU-hr -> cost per session.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a lightweight operational brief rather than a full paper. Wanted to surface actionable knobs quickly.
- Diego/Linh: please add raw CSV extracts and perf traces to GH PR referenced above (GH: redwood/serving-runtime#4128) so infra can run exact replays.
- If we like the direction, we should convert this into a reproducible notebook + small dashboard tile in Console (per-route session mix + suggested routing).

-- Asha (platform-engineering)
